newsitem.title: UK: UK Dec net bank mortgage lending rises 552 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK Dec net bank mortgage lending rises 552 mln stg.

text.p: Net lending for house purchases by major British banks rose a seasonally adjusted 552 million stg after a 606 million stg rise in November, the British Bankers' Association (BBA) said.
Unadjusted gross lending totalled 2.476 billion stg, seven percent down from November's 2.672 billion.

The number of new mortgage approvals fell an unadjusted 20 percent from November to 32,234, in line with the expected seasonal pattern, the BBA said. Their value was also down 20 percent to 1.883 billion stg.
BBA director-general Tim Sweeney said the outlook for the coming months was encouraging.
"The December figures held up well once account is taken of seasonal factors and in the final quarter of 1996 numbers of new approvals were some 40 percent higher than a year earlier," he said.
"Despite the possibility of some increase in interest rates in the months ahead, the signs are that mortgage lending and the housing market will continue to strengthen during the course of 1997."
